title: Low-power time-series summarizer and hover-latency fallback
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: High-density time-series views on the Console produce heavy DOM activity from per-point tooltip/legend updates and cause battery/CPU spikes on laptops and tablets. On slow devices or when the app is backgrounded, hover latency increases and screen readers get overwhelmed by repeated aria updates. Goal: design a progressive, device-aware summarizer and hover-fallback that preserves discoverability and keyboard/voice access while reducing DOM churn and paint activity.
design_notes: Introduce a small semantic summarizer module that lives alongside the canvas rendering layer: a terse, single-line textual summary updated at throttled intervals (default 250ms) and exposed via aria-live=polite for screen readers.

Legend condensation: when series count > 8 or when device hints low-power mode, switch to tokenized legend (compact chips) that reveal full labels on focus or via a collapse-expander control. Chips are implemented as lightweight buttons reusing existing token/button design tokens.

Hover-latency fallback: on pointer devices with input latency > 120ms (heuristic), disable per-point live tooltip rendering and show the summarizer instead; provide a prominent keyboard-accessible probe control to request an exact point tooltip (opens a small overlay modal).

Rendering strategy: keep heavy drawing on an offscreen canvas; only update DOM when the summarizer text changes. For interactions that absolutely need DOM (annotations, persistent highlights), batch DOM updates to requestAnimationFrame and coalesce changes every 200ms.

Accessibility: avoid aria-live spam by debouncing announcements and collapsing multiple rapid updates into a single concise phrase (e.g., "3 series, latest values: A 12.3, B 9.1..."). Provide an opt-in verbose mode in accessibility settings for power users who want every change announced.

Token mapping: add two new semantic tokens to the design system - chart.legend.compactBackground and chart.summarizer.textColor - mapped in light/dark/high-contrast themes. Ensure color token contrast meets 4.5:1 for small text in condensed legend chips.
Low-power asset mode: switch off animated gradients and drop shadow layers when batterySaver or prefers-reduced-motion is set; replace with flat tones using chart token palette.
Measurements: we expect DOM nodes reduced by ~65% for heavy dashboards and paint time decreased by ~30% on target devices (benchmarks in Acceptance Criteria).
acceptance_criteria: Throttled summarizer appears below canvas and reads a short summary via aria-live without creating more than one DOM update per 250ms under sustained high-frequency data streams.
When device is flagged low-power or series count > 8, legend automatically condenses to chip mode; keyboard users can tab into each chip and reveal full label with Enter/Space.
Hover fallback triggers on large event loop latency (>=120ms) and shows summarizer instead of per-point tooltip; explicit probe control opens detailed overlay with full point metadata.
Design tokens added for chart.legend.compactBackground and chart.summarizer.textColor are present in theme token files and pass color-contrast checks in light/dark/HC themes.

Benchmarks: on a mid-range ARM laptop (emulated), initial paint time for a 3k-point series view reduces by at least 25% and main-thread CPU usage drops by at least 30% compared to baseline; measurements captured in console-telemetry dashboard link below.
Docs: accessibility behavior, keyboard flows, and token adoption documented in the component readme and linked to the Console accessibility page.
tasks: Design: create Figma frames for condensed legend chips, summarizer copy variants (short, medium, verbose) and probe overlay UX
Engineering: implement summarizer API with options for throttleIntervalMs and verbosity; add device hint detection (battery/power/latency)
Engineering: add token entries to theme files and update CSS variables for compact legend and summarizer colors
QA: build automated accessibility checks for aria-live debouncing and keyboard reveal flows
Performance: create benchmark script and recording plan; add telemetry counters to Console dashboard
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Patel: Initial draft spec created after spike with Eng on 2026-02-17. Included measured sample rates and proposed 250ms throttle. Leaving open questions around exact latency threshold.

2026-02-25 Elliot Huang: Spike results look promising. Suggest lowering hover threshold to 100ms for mobile to keep UX responsive on touch-first devices. I'll prototype detection logic and share a demo next week.

2026-03-03 Priya Suresh (A11y): Strong preference for single concise announcement that summarizes top-three series; verbose mode optional. We should avoid announcing numeric deltas unless user requests it.
2026-03-08 Dan Rivera (Infra): Telemetry hooks added to the prototype branch — remember to mask any PII in summaries and ensure summarizer does not expose raw customer IDs.
2026-03-10 Elliot Huang: Implemented prototype branch (WIP) and uploaded bench CSV. Next steps: token mapping, color QA, and accessibility acceptance tests.
